approaches.name: Big data, open data portals and microdata systems for official statistics
approaches.description: The project pilots big data, builds open data portals and harmonized transmission architecture, and publishes anonymized microdata to modernize statistical production. Practices: Piloting Big Data processing for official statistics; SADC Integrated Trade Statistics System; Open Data Portals for SADC statistics with map analytics; Harmonized data transmission architecture for member NSOs; Migration and Tourism Information Systems in Zambia; National data portals disseminating anonymized micro-data; SDCMicro-based microdata anonymization and cataloging for open data access; Big Data analyses and indicator production pilots; Phone-based quarterly high-frequency household and enterprise surveys; Open data microdata library with anonymized datasets and publication calendar; Online microdata access from ZamStats web portal; Satellite imagery for rapid monitoring data production; Satellite imagery for rapid monitoring and data gap filling; satellite and call-record big data for adaptive statistics.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: Big Data piloted in official statistics - cue: 'piloting' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: It will primarily support NSOs to improve their ability to collect and produce statistical information by developing guidelines and delivering technical assistance for data collection from administrative records, expanding the use of specialized software, assisting development and maintenance of Statistical Business Registers, piloting processing Big Data for statistical purposes, delivering trainings for accessing and use of spatial information to collect census and survey data (GIS) through cartographic work, providing advanced training on sampling techniques, develop harmonized survey modules to collect household-level surveys to generate more data on informal sector, poverty, labor statistics, gender, migration, and so on.

extra_evidence.text: Under this sub-component, the SADC Secretariat’s statistics department will develop and implement SADC’s Integrated Trade Statistics System;

Open Data Portals for SADC Statistics with the latest dissemination technologies (analytics using maps, and so on); and develop and implement harmonized data transmissions procedures and architecture for Member country NSOs.

Lastly, in Zambia the project will also support administrative data systems, such as the development of a Migration Information System and a Tourism Information system, and the compilation of climate statistics.

The 50x2030 Initiative shall cover technical assistance costs related to data production (for example, survey program design, survey preparation, data collection and processing, and data dissemination including support for developing national data portals disseminating anonymized micro-data), strengthening data use (for example, data analysis, use of survey data in policy and program design, and so on), and capacity building (for example, training activities related to data production and data use, technical workshops, development of tools and methodologies).

The project will support a variety of mechanisms to achieve this, including strengthening skills in key methodologies and tools such as Data Documentation Initiative, microdata cataloging, anonymization protocols (for instance SdCMicro); the development of data dissemination strategies with key stakeholders, portals and redesigned NSO websites.33 The project also aims to develop forward and backward linkages between the NSO and line ministries to ultimately achieve open access and support evidence-based policymaking.
This not only makes data central to policymaking, but it also generates a data culture and raises the profile of national statistics strategies and the NSO.

Finally, the project will follow Recommendation 5 to implement coordinated actions so that World Bank operations benefit from Big Data’s insights and clients receive appropriate support for Big Data use by piloting several Big Data analyses and indicator production with SADC and several country NSOs.

Specifically, the project will support the continuation of socio-economic household surveys such as EPM (Enquête Périodique auprès des Ménages) in 2024 &2027 and the phone-based High Frequency Household Surveys (quarterly).
On the economic side, the project will support phone-based high frequency enterprise surveys (quarterly) on different topics, as well as the annual business survey.

This implies preparing and disseminating detailed and timely reports, as well as investing in open data by publishing indicators and tabulations and making freely available the anonymized datasets from each of these subcomponents in INSEED’s micro-data library, following a publication calendar.
One substantial improvement under this component is allowing microdata access from the web.
Currently data is only accessed by submitting an email request.
The microdata from all surveys financed by this project will be available online, as well as select surveys implemented in the last few years.

Similarly, the NSO will seek opportunities to incorporate information from satellite imagery to carry out rapid monitoring systems that enable timely and cost-effective production of data to be used by line ministries.

The project will also seek opportunities to use non-traditional data sources like satellite imagery to fill data gaps and carry out rapid monitoring to enable timely and cost-effective production of data.

This project will contribute to the design and development of initiatives that produce and collect data on frequent events such as climate shocks, price changes, economic agglomerations, among others, which can be measured through satellite imagery and rapid collection systems and that could benefit policy makers by providing real-time information on relevant areas.

Similarly, the NSO will seek opportunities to incorporate information from satellite imagery to carry out rapid monitoring systems that enable timely and cost-effective production of data to be used by line ministries.

The region could also benefit from using modern sources of Big Data – especially data from satellites and call records from phone – that allow a more adaptive approach for example in emergency situations caused by pandemics or natural disasters (see Annex 1 for more detailed description on the statistical capacity gaps in SADC).
